ENGINE IS A PT6A-34, VASAR STC FOR THE PRATT AND WHITNEY TURBINE. PILOT REPORTED A SURGE IN THE ENGINE DURING TAKEOFF AND A POWER LOSS. THE ENGINE RECOVERED QUICKLY AFTER THE POWER LOSS. THE AIRCRAFT WAS BEING RELOCATED FROM NOT FAR FROM THE MAIN HANGER, SO THE PILOT WAS ONLY IN THE AIR FOR A VERY SHORT TIME. THE AIRCRAFT WAS PUT IN THE HANGER, AND WE INVESTIGATED THE DISCREPANCY. LARGE ICE CHUNKS WERE FOUND ON THE LEFT AND RIGHT SIDES OF THE AIR INTAKE AREA AFT OF THE DIVERTER AND A SMALL AMOUNT OF ICE WAS ON THE BOTTOM OF THE AIR INTAKE. WE ARE BASED IN KETCHIKAN ALASKA AND THE AIRCRAFT WAS OUTSIDE PARKED FOR OVER A WEEK. IT HAS BEEN RAINING HEAVILY AND WATER SITS IN THE LOW SPOT OF THE INTAKE. THE TEMPERATURE DROPPED BELOW FREEZING AND HAS STAYED BELOW FREEZING. WHAT IT APPEARS HAPPENED IS THE WATER THAT DID NOT DRAIN OUT OF THE INTAKE FROZE, THEN WHEN ENOUGH POWER WAS APPLIED TO THE ENGINE THE LARGE, OVER AN INCH THICK PIECE OF ICE RELEASED ITSELF FROM THE INTAKE AND HIT THE AFT SCREEN AND BROKE INTO MANY PIECES. WE DOWNLOADED THE DATA FROM THE ELECTRONICS INTERNATIONAL MVP-50 AND COULD SEE THE EVENT. WE INSPECTED THE ENGINE AND DID NOT FIND ANY ISSUES OR DAMAGE CAUSED BYT HE ICE.

THIS IS A KING AIR 360 (N355GB)  -  AIRCRAFT DEPARTED KPDX ON 1/18/23 AT ROUGHLY 12:30 LOCAL WITH 8 PAX.
IT WAS RAINING AT THE FIELD AND THE TEMPERATURE WAS 6 DEGREES AT TOOK OFF.  (PILOT KNEW THIS FOR SURE BECAUSE HE TURNED ON ENGINE ANTI-ICE AND PROP DEICE PRIOR TO TAKE-OFF IN ANTICIPATION OF THEM BEING IN 5 DEGREE TEMPERATURE SHORTLY AFTER LIFTOFF.
CRUISING ALTITUDE WAS TO BE FL290 AND CREW RECEIVED A CONTINUOUS CLIMB ALL THE WAY UP.  THEY NEVER LEVELED OFF AT AN INTERMEDIATE ALTITUDE.  (THIS MAY HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO POSSIBLE ICING PROBLEMS INSIDE THE HORIZONTAL STABILIZER, IF THAT WAS THE CAUSE OF ALL OF THIS.)
CLIMB SPEED VARIED SOMEWHAT, BUT NEVER WENT BELOW MINIMUM ICING SPEED OF 140KTS.
SHORTLY AFTER LEVELING OFF AT FL290, THE RED TRIM LIGHT LIT UP ON THE PANEL.  THE PILOT DECIDED TO DISCONNECT THE AUTOPILOT TO SEE IF HE COULD MANIPULATE THE TRIM IS SOME WAY TO ELIMINATE THE TRIM LIGHT.  THE TRIM WHEEL WAS COMPLETELY FROZEN AND LOCKED IN PLACE.  NEITHER PILOT OR AUTOPILOT WAS ABLE TO ROTATE IT.  
THE PILOT FOUND THAT THERE WAS A RATHER EXTREME LEVEL OF UP TRIM DIALED IN.  THE AIRCRAFT JUMPED A BIT AND REQUIRED QUITE A BIT OF FORCE TO MAINTAIN LEVEL ALTITUDE (I.E. KEEP IT FROM CLIMBING).  THE PILOT SAID HE WOULD PUT THE PRESSURE AT PERHAPS 50 POUNDS OF FORCE.
THE PIC TASKED THE COPILOT TO SEE IF HE COULD FIND ANYTHING IN THE AIRCRAFT QUICK REFERENCE GUIDE (ABNORMAL AND EMERGENCY PROCEDURES).  HE COULD FIND NOTHING.
PILOT INFORMED ATC OF CONTROL PROBLEMS AND REQUESTED A BLOCK ALTITUDE OF FL280 - FL300.
PILOT THEN DISCONNECTED THE AUTO-THROTTLES AND ATTEMPTED TO IMPROVE CONTROL BY SLOWING THE AIRCRAFT SPEED (I.E. DRIVE THE AIRSPEED CLOSER TO WHERE THE AIRPLANE WAS TRIMMED).
THE CREW PUSHED THE TRIM DISCONNECT ON THE CONTROL WHEEL - NO IMPACT.
PILOT HAD COPILOT PULL THE TRIM BREAKER - NO IMPACT.
IN THE END, NOTHING RESOLVED THE ISSUE OF THE FROZEN TRIM WHEEL AND RESULTING LACK OF CONTROLLABILITY.  THE SLOWER AIRSPEED HELPED TO SOME EXTENT, BUT THE PLANE REQUIRED BOTH ARMS TO HOLD THE NOSE DOWN.
CREW REQUESTED TO RETURN TO KPDX AND DECLARED AN EMERGENCY ON ROUTE BACK TO THE AIRPORT.
THE TRIM WHEEL BECAME MOVABLE AGAIN SOMEWHERE AROUND 1,000 TO 2,000 FEET.  THIS CORRESPONDED TO TEMPERATURE READINGS GOING ABOVE FREEZING.
PILOT BRIEFED BOTH THE FAA AND THE NTSB ON WHAT HAPPENED.
TEXTRON WAS CALLED AND THEY SENT OUT AND AOG CONTRACT TEAM TO LOOK OVER THE AIRCRAFT WITHIN A FEW DAYS.
MAINTENANCE SUSPECTED ICE WORKED ITS WAY INTO THE HORIZONTAL STABILIZER THROUGH ACCESS PANELS ON TOP OF THE STABILIZER.  THIS STABILIZER IS A MIRROR IMAGE OF THE OTHER SIDE.  THE OTHER SIDE HAS THE ACCESS PANELS ON THE BOTTOM IF IT.  THE SIDE AFFECTED HAS THE ACCESS PANELS ON THE TOP.  AFTER TALKING WITH TEXTRON THEY SAID THAT THERE WERE SIMILAR ISSUES WITH OLDER 300 OR 350 MODELS AND THIS WAS ADDRESSED BY ISSUING A CIRCULAR AND CHANGING A GREASE TYPE AND AN ADDITIONAL ITEM DURING AN INSPECTION.  THEY SAID THE 360 MODEL CAME WITH THE NEW GREASE FROM THE FACTORY.  WE WERE ALSO TOLD THAT THIS IS THE FIRST REPORT OF THIS HAPPENING TO A 360 MODEL.
AFTER LENGTHY DISCUSSION WITH TEXTRON, THEY INFORMED US THAT “THEIR” EXPERTS LOOKED INTO THIS MATTER AND DEEMED THAT IT “DID NOT AFFECT THE SAFETY OF SLIGHT”.  THIS IS OBVIOUSLY UNACCEPTABLE AND COULD HAVE EASILY INJURED OR KILLED SOMEONE.  WE WERE TOLD THEY WOULD KEEP LOOKING INTO THINGS BUT THAT THERE SEEMED TO BE NO NEED TO ISSUE AND AD OR ANY OTHER PRIORITY RESPONSE.

THE FLOW DIVIDER ON TOP OF THE ENGINE AT THE SPINE HAS A SMALL COMPENSATION HOLE ABOVE THE DIAPHRAGM. IF THE DIAPHRAGM HAS A PERFORATION, RAW FUEL WILL RISE ABOVE THE DIAPHRAGM AND SPEW FROM THIS HOLE AND THUS CAUSE AND EXTREME FIRE HAZARD. I HAVE OBSERVED THIS EFFECT ON TWO ENGINE RUNS WITH DIFFERENT FLOW DIVIDERS. I KNOW OF NO STC/AD TO CORRECT THIS CONDITION. A SMALL TUBE LEADING TO BELOW THE ENGINE BAY WOULD CORRECT THIS UNSAFE CONDITION.I SUSPECT THIS CONDITION IS PRESENT ON MANY AIRCRAFT---I ALSO OBSERVED THIS HOLE ON A BARON FLOW DIVIDER. THE SERVICE MANUAL DOES NOT SPECIFY A TIME COMPLIANCE CHANGE.

PER PILOT:  DURING OUR FLIGHT TODAY FROM PHL-MMUN WE SUFFERED LOSE OF PRESSURIZATION AT FL430. AT THE TIME OF OCCURRENCE WE WERE ABOUT 150 MILES OFF THE COAST OF FLORIDA. 
WHILE CRUISING AT FL430 I STARTED FEELING THE AIRCRAFT DEPRESSURIZING BUT THE PRESSURE CHANGE IN OUR EARS. WE IMMEDIATELY SAW ON THE SCREEN THAT THE CABIN STARTED TO DUMP ITSELF AT A RATE OF ABOUT 2500 FPM. SUBSEQUENTLY WE GOT A CABIN DELTA P WARNING MSG (DELTA P WAS 9.2-9.3). WE INITIATED AN EMERGENCY DECENT. ATC WANTED TO GIVE AN ALTITUDE AROUND FL350 DUE TO TRAFFIC AROUND US. THEREFORE, I DECLARED AN EMERGENCY AND CONTINUED THE DECENT TO 14,000FT.
DURING OUR DECENT WE FOLLOWED THE QRH FOR THE CAS MSG. THE PROCEDURE REQUIRED US TO USE MANUAL PRESSURIZATION. WE MANAGED TO CONTROL THE CABIN ALTITUDE AROUND FL300.
I DECIDED TO DIVERT TO A U.S AIRPORT SO THE AIRPLANE WON’T BE STUCK AT A FOREIGN COUNTRY. 
LANDING WAS UNEVENTFUL. WE TAXIED IN TO ATLANTIC FBO AND UNLOADED THE PAX.                                                                                                                                        MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL WAS IMMEDIATELY DISPATCHED AND MET THE AIRCRAFT AT THE FBO. AIRCRAFT LRU NVM WERE DOWNLOADED AND SUBMITTED TO BOMBARDIER CRC FOR REVIEW AND RECOMMENDATIONS. BOMBARDIER SUGGESTED ORDERING AN OUTFLOW VALVE AS A PREVENTATIVE MEASURE. PERFORMED TROUBLESHOOTING STEPS ON THE IASC 1 AND IASC 2 ON THE GROUND. THERE ARE 4 SUSPECTED COMPONENTS THAT COULD CAUSE THIS ISSUE, THE IASC 1/2, THE SAFETY VALVES AND THE OUTFLOW VALVE. DURING TROUBLESHOOTING THE TECHNICIANS FOUND A BIT OF FOAM MATERIAL IN THE SAFETY VALVE IN THE BAGGAGE COMPARTMENT. UNCLEAR ON WHERE THE FOAM CAME FROM AT THIS TIME. PENDING FURTHER REVIEW OF THE STEPS TAKEN WE WILL AWAIT DIRECTION FROM CRC FOR FURTHER TROUBLESHOOTING STEPS.

ON 4/15/23, N662AR FLEW FROM KVNY TO KLAS. AS THE CREW COMPLETED A NORMAL LANDING OF THE AIRCRAFT IN LAS, THEY WERE INSTRUCTED TO TURN OFF ON A HIGH SPEED TAXI WAY AND PROCEED TO PARKING. THE TRS WERE DEPLOYED AND WORKING NORMALLY. AS THE TURN WAS INITIATED AND TRS STOWED THE CREW REPORTED THE STEERING DID NOT RESPOND AND THE BRAKES HAD LITTLE TO NO PEDAL FEEL WHEN PRESSED. THEY WERE COMING UP ON ANOTHER AIRCRAFT THAT WAS AHEAD OF THEM AND ELECTED TO USE THE EMERGENCY BRAKING (EMER AIR) WHICH SLOWED THE AIRCRAFT WHILE THE AIRCRAFT IN FRONT WAS ABLE TO MOVE ON AND WAS CLEAR. WITH ENOUGH RAMP SPACE AND NO OTHER AIRCRAFT NEARBY, THE AIRCRAFT WAS SLOWING ON ITS OWN INTO A LH TURN, THE CAPTAIN LET IT CONTINUE ON THE TURN WHICH SLOWED THE AIRCRAFT ALMOST TO A STOP. HE THEN CAME TO A COMPLETE STOP WITH A SMALL INPUT OF EMER AIR. HE THEN FELT SOLID BRAKE PRESSURE RESISTANCE ON THE BRAKE PEDALS AND THE STEERING STARTED WORKING AGAIN. THE AIRCRAFT WAS PARKED AT THE FBO WITH STEERING AND BRAKING ACTION WORKING NORMALLY. ON 4/17 ATI JET MAINTENANCE WAS DISPATCHED TO LAS TO INSPECT THE AIRCRAFT. NO DISCREPANCIES WERE FOUND. BRAKING WAS NORMAL, STEERING SYSTEM ALSO FOUND TO BE WORKING NORMALLY. A FERRY PERMIT WAS GRANTED AND A NORMAL TAXI/TAKEOFF DEPARTING LAS WITH THE SAME IN ELP. NO DETERMINATION HAS BEEN MADE AS TO WHAT CAUSED THE ISSUES IN LAS. ALL ANTI SKID COMPONENTS WILL BE TESTED/INSPECTED AS WELL AS THE STEERING SYSTEM COMPUTER, SERVO AND OTHER RELATED ITEMS.

WE RECEIVED A REQUEST FOR AN IFT IN OUR LOCAL AREA. AFTER EACH CREW MEMBER COMPLETED THEIR WALKAROUND WE BOARDED THE AIRCRAFT AND I STARTED THE AIRCRAFT. THE STARTUP WAS NORMAL AND I PREPARED FOR TAKEOFF. THAT EVENING THE WIND AT BASE WAS LIGHT, MAYBE 4-6 KNOTS, AND COMING FROM THE AIRCRAFTS 2 O'CLOCK POSITION. AFTER PICKUP I DID A PEDAL TURN INTO THE WIND AND CONDUCTED A BEAUTIFULLY SMOOTH TAKEOFF. SHORTLY AFTER TAKEOFF AND DURING THE CLIMB THE CREW MEMBER IN THE AFT-FWD FACING SEAT REVEALED THEY HAD A SUDDEN SMELL OF FUEL IN THE CABIN. WITH THE SUDDEN ONSET OF THE FUMES AND THE KNOWLEDGE THE KNOWLEDGE #2 FUEL CONTROL WAS REPLACED WITHIN THE LAST TWO WEEKS I DECIDE TO ABORT THE FLIGHT AND RETURN TO BASE. I INFORMED AIRCOM OF OUR NEW ABORT STATUS AND REASON. UPON MAKING THE LEFT-HAND TURN TO RTB THE CREW MEMBER IN THE CO-PILOT SEAT INDICATED THEY COULD ALSO SMELL FUEL NOW. THE LANDING BACK AT BASE WAS SILKY, EFFICIENT AND WITHOUT INCIDENT. AFTER SHUTDOWN I CALLED OUR MECHANIC AND AIRCOM TO ADVISE THEM OF OUR SITUATION. OUR SELFLESS MECHANIC COME OUT AND INSPECTED THE SYSTEM FOR ANY LEAKS OR COMPROMISES, NONE NOTED. FOLLOWING AN EXTENDED GROUND RUN NOTHING WAS DETECTED.

AT LEAST FOUR DIFFERENT TIMES IN AT LEAST TWO DIFFERENT PC12S, WITH THE MOST OCCURRENCE RECENT BEING JUL 12, 2023, ONE PITOT TUBE BECAME BLOCKED DURING CRUISE FLIGHT. THIS RESULTS IN A LOSS OF PRIMARY INSTRUMENTS ON ONE SIDE OF THE AIRPLANE, USUALLY THE LOSS OF THE STANDBY INSTRUMENT AS WELL, AND DISENGAGEMENT OF THE AUTOPILOT. I CAN TEMPORARILY REMEDY THE PROBLEM BY PULLING THE ADAHRS CIRCUIT BREAKER ON THE BLOCKED SIDE OF THE AIRPLANE AND RE-INITIALIZING THE AUTOPILOT. IN THE MOST RECENT INCIDENT, I DESCENDED BELOW THE FREEZING LEVEL TO CLEAR THE BLOCKAGE BEFORE CLIMBING BACK UP TO CRUISE ALTITUDE. IN EACH INCIDENT, I HAD OUR SERVICE CENTER LOOK AT THE AIRPLANE. THEY FOUND ALL DEICING SYSTEMS TO BE WORKING NORMALLY, AND NO WATER IN THE PITOT/STATIC SYSTEM. I SUSPECT THAT UNDER CERTAIN CONDITIONS, WATER ACCUMULATES IN THE PITOT STATIC SYSTEM AND FREEZES WHEN THE OAT DROPS LOW ENOUGH EVEN IF ALL DEICE AND ANTI-ICE SYSTEMS ARE FUNCTIONING AS DESIGNED. IT SEEMS LIKE THIS COULD BE QUITE DANGEROUS, AND IT IS HAPPENING WITH ENOUGH REGULARITY THAT I'D LIKE SOMEONE TO KNOW ABOUT IT.

ON TEN OCCASIONS SINCE 2020, PILOTS REPORTED THE UNCOMMANDED INFLATION OF ALL THEIR DEICE BOOTS AT ONCE DURING TAKE-OFF. ON EVERY OCCASION, THEY WERE ABLE TO RESET THE SYSTEM AND RESTORE THE PROPER OPERATION OF THE BOOTS. THE SYSTEM RESUMED PROPER SEQUENTIAL INFLATION AND DEFLATION.  ON THE FIRST OCCASION, WE WERE ABLE TO TROUBLESHOOT A DISTRIBUTOR VALVE, P/N: 1532-10C, AND FOUND THAT IT HAD BEEN CHARD/ BURNED BY AN OEM TANIS-STYLE HEATING PAD ATTACHED TO THE VALVE BODY INTENDED TO PREVENT THE VALVE FROM ICING UP. THE VALVE BODIES ARE MADE FROM A BAKELITE/ PLASTIC MATERIAL.  ON EVERY SUBSEQUENT OCCASION, WE FOUND THE DISTRIBUTOR VALVE HAD THE SAME HEAT DAMAGE THOUGH TO A FAR LESSER EXTENT. THIS INDICATED THAT THE FIRST DISCREPANCY WAS ONGOING FOR FAR LONGER THAN WE INITIALLY THOUGHT AND IT WAS LIKELY THE FIRST TIME PILOTS NOTICED SOMETHING WAS WRONG WITH THE DE-ICING SYSTEM. WE HAVE WORKED FAITHFULLY WITH VIKING TO MITIGATE THE DAMAGE BY MODIFYING THE PROCEDURAL USE OF THE VALVE HEAT SO THAT HEAT IS NOT ON WHEN IT IS NOT NEEDED. UNFORTUNATELY, THIS HAS ONLY DELAYED THE INEVITABLE AND THE VALVE PROBLEM ALWAYS RETURNS.  IN OUR STRUGGLES, WE DISCOVERED THAT THE APPROVED PART NUMBER DISTRIBUTOR VALVES FROM THE DHC-6-100 THROUGH 300 DEICE SYSTEMS, P/N: 1532-3C, ARE MADE OF ALUMINUM. THE DHC-6-400(N814SS) CALLS FOR THE PLASTIC DISTRIBUTOR VALVE, P/N: 1532-10C. IN OUR DISCUSSIONS WITH VIKING, NOW DEHAILLAND, WE WERE UNABLE TO DETERMINE WHY THEY STARTED USING PLASTIC INSTEAD OF ALUMINUM OTHER THAN COST SAVINGS. I BELIEVE THIS IS A CRITICAL MISTAKE. THE ALUMINUM-BODIED VALVES ARE IDEAL FOR HEAT DISSIPATION AND DEICING WHERE THE PLASTIC BODIES CONCENTRATE HEAT TO ONE LOCATION AND BURN THE ASSEMBLY. THIS IS S DEFICIENCY IN DESIGN. I AM REQUESTING RELIEF BY ALLOWING THE ALUMINUM-BODIED DISTRIBUTOR VALVES TO BE USED IN -400 SERIES AIRCRAFT.  ORIGINAL SUBMISSION DATE: 7/13/2023

WHILE PERFORMING A GEAR INSTALLATION PROCEDURE ON A HAWKER 800XP AN INSPECTOR INADVERTENTLY UNCOVERED A MISTAKE IN THE HAWKER 750 MAINTENANCE MANUAL. PROCEDURE (4) (A)(B) “MAIN GEAR INSTALLATION,” AND THE PRODUCTION INSPECTOR NOTICED THE TORQUE CALLED OUT WAS IN FOOT POUNDS.  WE RECENTLY HAD INSTALLED MAIN GEAR ON HAWKER 750 S/N HB-69 AND HE SEEMED TO REMEMBER THAT THE SAME BOLTS WERE TORQUED IN INCH POUNDS, WHICH WE HAVE NOW CONFIRMED.  HB69 WAS BROUGHT BACK INTO THE FACILITY AND RETORQUED TO FOOT POUNDS AFTER SUBMITTING THIS ERROR TO TEXTRON WHO SAID A MAINTENANCE MANUAL REVISION WOULD BE IN THE WORKS.  OUR CONCERN IS HOW MANY OTHER HAWKER 750'S HAVE THEIR MAIN LANDING GEAR TRUNNION ATTACHMENT BOLTS TORQUED TO 72-82 INCH POUNDS WHEN THEY ARE SUPPOSED TO BE TORQUED TO 72-82 FOOT POUNDS WITH THIS MAINTENANCE MANUAL ERROR.  REFERENCE HAWKER 750, 800XP AND 900XP MAINTENANCE MANUALS CHAPTER 32-10-12-401 STEP 4.A. PROCEDURE (4) (A)(B) “MAIN GEAR INSTALLATION."  YOU WILL FIND THE HAWKER 800XP AND 900XP TORQUES ARE IN FOOT POUNDS FOR THIS PROCEDURE YET THE 750 IS IN INCH POUNDS FOR THE SAME MAIN LANDING GEAR. ON THURSDAY, 8/3/23, FLIGHT CYO602, N600SJ WAS AT CRUISE ALTITUDE, ENROUTE FROM KSDL TO KBFI WHEN THE CREW NOTICED THE LH & RH HYDRAULIC PRESSURE WARNING LIGHTS ILLUMINATE. VIA WIFI INSTALLED ON THE AIRCRAFT, THE CAPTAIN CALLED ATI JET MAINTENANCE TO INFORM THEM OF THE SITUATION. MAINTENANCE INSTRUCTED THE CAPTAIN TO LAND. THE CREW CHOSE KPDX, PORTLAND OREGON, AS IT WAS THE CLOSEST AIRPORT WITH A LONG RUNWAY. THE CREW CONTACTED PDX AND STARTED THE DECENT. AT 20,000 FT, THE FLAPS WERE LOWERED TO RECOMMENDED SETTING AND THE LANDING GEAR WAS EXTENDED NORMALLY. THE HYDRAULIC PRESSURE INDICATOR HAD BEEN HOLDING STEADY AT NORMAL OPERATING PRESSURE SO THE DIVERSION AT FIRST WAS PRECAUTIONARY. SHORTLY AFTER THE GEAR WAS EXTENDED THE PRESSURE AT THE INDICATOR STARTED DROPPING. THE PRESSURE WENT TO ZERO AND THE CREW CHOSE TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY IN TO PDX. AS THEY PASSED THROUGH 5000 FT, THE PRESSURE CAME BACK UP TO 600 PSI AND FLUCTUATED FROM 6-800 PSI ALL THE WAY DOWN THROUGH LANDING AND PARKING. THE AIRCRAFT WAS LANDED SAFELY AT PDX AIRPORT AND TAXIED TO PARKING ON NORMAL BRAKING. LOCAL MAINTENANCE WAS CALLED AND IDENTIFIED THE LEAK TO BE COMING FROM THE ENGINE DRIVEN HYDRAULIC PUMP PRESSURE LINES, LH & RH WERE LEAKING. ATI MAINTENANCE CALLED LEARJET TECH SUPPORT FOR SUGGESTIONS AS TO WHAT ELSE NEEDED TO BE INSPECTED IN THIS SITUATION. THEY HAD SEEN THIS SAME SITUATION IN OTHER LEARS SO WHEN ATI MAINTENANCE ARRIVED INTO PDX THEY FOCUSED ON THE LEARJET TECHS RECOMMENDATIONS. THE HYDRAULIC RESERVOIR PRESSURE CHECK VALVE WAS FOUND STUCK OPEN WHICH CAUSED THE FLUID IN THE SYSTEM TO AERATE AND CAVITATE THE PUMPS UP AT ALTITUDE. ALSO CAUSING SHOCK IN THE FLOW OF THE PRESSURE SIDE OF THE SYSTEM. WHICH CAUSED THE FLEX LINE AT THE HYD PUMP TO LEAK. ATI MAINTENANCE REMOVED AND INSPECTED THE PRESSURE AND RETURN HYDRAULIC FILTERS, NO CONTAMINATION FOUND. BOTH FILTERS WERE REPLACED WITH NEW. BOTH ENGINE DRIVEN HYDRAULIC PUMPS WERE REPLACED, BOTH LH & RH PRESSURE AND RETURN LINES WERE REPLACED, THE HYDRAULIC PRESSURE REGULATOR,  PRESSURE CHECK VALVE AND PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE WERE REPLACED. THE AIRCRAFT WAS JACKED FOR GEAR SWINGS, ALL NORMAL. ALL HYDRAULIC SYSTEMS WERE TESTED AND FOUND TO BE IN NORMAL WORKING CONDITION. THE AIRCRAFT WAS RELEASED TO SERVICE AND A TEST FLIGHT WAS COMPLETED WITH NO ISSUES REPORTED.

ON TUESDAY AUGUST 8TH AT APPROXIMATELY 2:45 PST N503JA TOOK OFF FROM KFUL ON RUNWAY 24. APPROX. 8 MIN INTO THE FLIGHT THE AIRCRAFT WAS LEVELED OFF AND TRAVELING AT APPROX. 150KTS. THE PILOT REPORTED THE AT THAT APPROX. 8 MIN MARK AFTER TAKING OFF THE AIRCRAFT BEGAN TO OCELLATE/PORPOISE UP AND DOWN VIOLENTLY. THE YOKE MOVED IN AND OUT SO VIOLENTLY THAT HE COULD HARDLY HOLD ON TO THE YOKE. IN FACT THE FRICTION OF THE YOKE GOING IN AND OUT RUBBED ALL THE SKIN OFF OF HIS HANDS. THE PILOT INITIALLY THOUGH THAT THE ENGINE WAS COMING APART SO HE PULLED THE MIXTURE AND KILLED THE ENGINE. HE CALLED FULLERTON TOWER DECLARED AND EMERGENCY AND SQUAWKED 7700.  WE WAS ABLE TO LAND SUCCESSFULLY AT KFUL ONTO RUNWAY 24 AT APPROX. 3 PM PST. IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE RH STABILATOR BROKE IN HALF IN FLIGHT AT THE MAIN AND AFT SPAR. IT THEN CAUSED EXCESSIVE PRESSURE ON THE BOLT THAT HOLDS THE STABILATOR TRIM TABS TOGETHER AND THAT BOLT SHEERED. THIS CAUSED BOTH STABILATOR TRIM TABS TO FLUTTER VIOLENTLY. THE LH STABILATOR WAS DAMAGED FROM THE LH TRIM TAB HITTING THE STABILATOR DURING THE FLUTTER. THERE IS A SYMMETRICAL DEFORMATION ON BOTH HE RH AND LH TRIM TABS WITCH SHOW THEY WERE TOGETHER WHEN THE INCIDENT OCCURRED. THIS COULD HAVE VERY EASY RESULTED IN A CATASTROPHIC IN FLIGHT BREAKUP AND LOSS OF LIFE. ON A SCALE OF 1 TO 10 I PUT THIS ON AN EXTREME 10 OF IMPORTANCE FOR REVIEW. THE DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT FROM THE RH STABILATOR FAILURE HAS CAUSED SEVERE DAMAGE TO THE LH STABILATOR AS WELL AS BOTH RH AND LH STABILATOR TRIM TABS. MY NORMAL CROSS CHECK IDENTIFIED A DISPARITY IN #1 AND #2 ENGINE OIL TEMPERATURE OF APPROXIMATELY 12 DEGREES C AFTER ABOUT 5 MINUTES OF FLIGHT AT CRUISE. ABOUT 12 MILES SOUTH OF THE CITY OF LAS CRUCES, NM I NOTICED THE #2 OIL TEMP CLIMB ACCELERATE SO I REDUCED POWER TO VH HOPING THAT WOULD COOL THE ENGINE A BIT.  I SIMULTANEOUSLY MADE A RIGHT TURN TOWARD LAS CRUCES AIRPORT TO EXECUTE A PRECAUTIONARY LANDING. REDUCED POWER DID NOT HALT THE OIL TEMPERATURE CLIMB SO WHEN IT HIT THE OIL TEMP LIMIT THEN I PLACED #2 ENGINE INTO IDLE.  #1 ENGINE TOOK UP THE LOAD NICELY AND PROVIDED SUFFICIENT POWER TO KEEP THE AIRCRAFT AIRBORNE THE 12 MILES BACK TO THE AIRPORT.  #2 OIL TEMPERATURE DID DROP SIGNIFICANTLY SO I DECIDED TO KEEP THE ENGINE OPERATING AT IDLE IN ORDER TO UTILIZE IT UPON LANDING SINCE WE WERE STILL VERY HEAVY.  EVERYTHING LOOKED GOOD ON FINAL APPROACH SO AT 50 KTS AND 50 FEET ABOVE THE RUNWAY I PLACED THE #2 ENGINE BACK TO FLY AND LANDED THE AIRCRAFT NORMALLY WITH NO FURTHER INCIDENT.
AFTER TAKEOFF THE CREWMEMBER IN THE CABIN REPORTED A STRONG JET FUEL ODOR.  INSPECTED AIRCRAFT AND ENGINE, NO FUEL LEAK DETECTED.

WE OPERATE/OWN 4 CITATION 680A LATITUDES FOR 5 YEARS NOW.  OVER THAT TIME WE HAVE SEEN NUMEROUS FAILURES OF THE EMERGENCY ESCAPE PATH LIGHTING SYSTEM.  THE FAILURE COMES DOWN TO THE EMERGENCY LIGHTING POWER PACKS.  THERE ARE 4 OF THESE PACKS IN THE LATITUDE EACH PACK OPERATING A SEPARATE ZONE IN THE CABIN.  TWO YEARS AGO CESSNA CHANGED THE PROCEDURE FOR CHECKING THESE POWER PACKS FROM A 3 YEAR REQUIREMENT TO A 12 MONTH INSPECTION UNDER TASK 33-50-00-961 WHICH IS A CAPACITY FUNCTIONAL CHECK OF THE BATTERIES IN THE POWER PACKS.  THIS CHECK WAS REDUCED TO 12 MONTHS TO HELP REMOVE THE MEMORY OF THE NICAD CELLS.  OUR OPERATION HAS SEEN A VERY HIGH RATE OF UNSCHEDULED REMOVAL OF THESE PACKS.  MOST ONLY LASTING 18 MONTHS BEFORE FAILURE.  BECAUSE OF THIS WE ELECTED TO SHORTEN THE INTERVAL TO 6 MONTHS TO TRY TO GET MORE LIFE OUT OF THESE PACKS AND GIVE US SOME INDICATION OF A PREMATURE FAILURE.  NONE OF THIS HAS LENGTHENED THE RELIABILITY OF THESE PACKS.  WHAT IS MOST DISTURBING IS THAT ONE PACK IN A ZONE CAN CAUSE A COMPETE LOSS OF THE ESCAPE PATH LIGHTING.  ZONE 1 AND ZONE 4 PACKS ARE CONSIDERED TO BE ESSENTIAL PACKS.  POWER FROM THE #1 PACK WILL ENERGIZE THE RELAY TO TURN ON THE ESCAPE PATH LIGHTING IN THE ARM POSITION, THE #4 PACK POWERS THE SAME RELAY FOR THE ON POSITION.  IT IS POSSIBLE TO HAVE A PACK FAIL WERE IT WILL TURN ON THE EMER LIGHTS BUT DOES NOT HAVE ENOUGH POWER TO ENERGIZE THE RELAY CAUSING A SYSTEM WIDE FAILURE.  THE ON POSITION IS NEVER TESTED IN THE PREFLIGHT CHECK.

BACK IN 2016, GULFSTREAM ISSUED CB 126, WHICH HAD OPERATORS REPLACE THE RIGHT ENGINE HYDRAULIC PUMP DEPRESSURIZATION VALVE CONNECTOR DUE TO FAILURE OF THE CONNECTOR PER ROLLS ROYCE SB BR700-71-900578. IN ADDITION, GULFSTREAM ISSUED CB 127 TO INSPECT THE RIGHT ENGINE HYDRAULIC PUMP DEPRESSURIZATION VALVE CONNECTORS FOR DETERIORATION. WHY IS THIS IMPORTANT? IN THE EVENT THAT AN INFLIGHT ENGINE RESTART IS REQUIRED, THE DEPRESSURIZATION VALVE UNLOADS THE HYDRAULIC PUMP SO THAT THE HP SPOOL CAN SPIN FREELY.  CB 126 AND CB 127 APPLY TO SERIAL NUMBERS 6003 THROUGH 6171, 6172 AND 6175. BY NOW, ALL OF THESE AIRCRAFT HAVE COMPLIED WITH THESE CBS.  WE RECENTLY DISCOVERED ONE OF OUR AIRCRAFT (G650ER, S/N 6397) HAD ITS HYDRAULIC PUMP DEPRESSURIZATION VALVE CONNECTOR TO BE DETERIORATED AND DISCONNECTED. WE HAD GULFSTREAM SAVANNAH REPAIR THE HARNESS ACCORDINGLY. I SPOKE WITH ROLLS ROYCE, AND THEY WERE SURPRISED BY THIS . . . AS WERE WE.  AFTER FURTHER RESEARCH BY OUR TEAM, IT APPEARS THAT THE HARNESS GOING TO THE RH ENGINE HYDRAULIC PUMP HAS A LOT OF LENGTH THAT IS UNSUPPORTED AND AS IT SUSPENDS FREELY.  THE NACELLE SYSTEM HAS AN AIR VENT LOCATED ON THE LOWER COWL DOOR, TOWARD THE FRONT END THAT CAUSES THE HARNESS TO VIBRATE.  CONSEQUENTLY, THE VIBRATION CAUSED BY THE AIRFLOW ON THE HARNESS CAUSES TREMENDOUS STRESS ON THE CONNECTOR, WHICH CAUSES THEM TO FAIL.  SINCE IT IS VERY EASY TO PERFORM A DETAILED INSPECTION OF THE RESPECTIVE CONNECTOR, WE DECIDED TO START INSPECTING THIS CONNECTOR AT EVERY 1A INTERVAL.  WE REMOVE THE CONNECTOR, INSPECT FOR ARCING AND DAMAGE TO THE HYDRAULIC PUMP RECEPTACLE.  SEVERAL OF MY COLLEAGUES ARE ALSO FINDING FAILED CONNECTORS AND DAMAGED HYDRAULIC PUMPS.  THEREFORE, I STRONGLY RECOMMEND GULFSTREAM MAINTAINABILITY CONSIDER ADDING THIS REQUIREMENT TO THE RESPECTIVE CH.05-20-00 SCHEDULE.

AS THE AIRCRAFT WAS PASSING THROUGH 24,000 FEET, I NOTICED THE OIL PRESSURE ON THE RIGHT ENGINE WAS STARTING TO DECREASE AT A NOTICEABLE RATE. I INFORMED FT WORTH CENTER OF THE SITUATION AND SAID I NEEDED TO LAND AT THE CLOSEST AIRPORT. THAT AIRPORT BEING KCRT. I INITIATED AN EMERGENCY DESCENT AND WHEN ON A 6 MILE FINAL TO THE AIRPORT THE RED WARNING LIGHT FOR OIL PRESSURE ILLUMINATED. I PULLED THE RIGHT ENGINE THROTTLE TO IDLE AND NOTICED THE OIL PRESSURE RISE AND THE WARNING LIGHT EXTINGUISH. I ELECTED TO LEAVE THE ENGINE RUNNING AT THIS TIME. ON SHORT FINAL THE WARNING LIGHT REILLUMINATED. ONCE I WAS ON THE RUNWAY I SHUTDOWN THE RIGHT ENGINE AND TAXIED INTO THE RAMP AREA. UPON EXITING THE AIRCRAFT I CHECKED THE OIL LEVEL AND THE DIPSTICK SHOWED NO OIL. I WAITED 30 MINUTES FOR THE ENGINE TO COOL AND CHECKED THE OIL LEVEL AGAIN AND STILL NO OIL WAS EVIDENT ON THE DIPSTICK. THE AIRCRAFT ENGINES HAD BEEN SERVICED THE PREVIOUS WEEK BY STEVENS AEROSPACE. I CALLED THEM TO INFORM THEM OF THE SITUATION AND THEY SENT A MOBILE AOG UNIT THAT AFTERNOON. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE MAGNETIC SEAL THAT WAS REPLACED THE PREVIOUS WEEK WAS DEFECTIVE. AFTER CONSULTING WITH THE ENGINE MANUFACTURER IT WAS DECIDED THAT THE BEST COURSE OF ACTION WAS TO REPLACE THE GEARBOX WITH A NEW STYLE, WHICH WOULD ELIMINATE THE NEED FOR THE SEALS. THE ENGINE WAS TEST RUN AND RETURNED TO SERVICE AFTER THE GEAR BOX WAS REPLACED.

WE CONTINUE TO LOOK THESE (AND OTHER) DISCREPANCIES DURING OUR INCOMING INSPECTION PROCESS AS WELL AS DURING OUR ASSEMBLY PROCESS.

THE HELICOPTER OVER CORRECTED THEN STARTED TO ROTATE TO THE LEFT BECAUSE OF THE PEDAL INPUT AND HAD TO CORRECT WITH RIGHT PEDAL. IT FELT LIKE I WAS FIGHTING THE FOLLOW ON TRIM AND HAD SEVERAL BACK AND FORTH INPUTS TRYING TO MAINTAIN HEADING. AT THIS POINT, I ELECTED TO PERFORM A HOVERING AUTO, RATHER THEN CONTINUE TO FIGHT THE PEDALS AND TRY TO LAND ON THE RAMP. ON 10/20/2023, N812RP WAS DEPARTING KSAT WITH PASSENGERS HEADING TO KELP. SHORTLY AFTER TAKEOFF, THE CREW NOTICED THE DUAL BLEED LIGHTS HAD ILLUMINATED. AFTER RUNNING THROUGH THE AIRCRAFT CHECKLIST, THE LIGHTS REMAINED ON AND THE CREW DECIDED TO RETURN TO KSAT. ANOTHER ATI AIRCRAFT WAS DISPATCHED WITH MECHANICS AND TO CONTINUE THE TRIP FOR THE PASSENGERS. ATI MAINTENANCE RAN THE ENGINES AND FOUND A BLOWN SEAL IN THE PNEUMATIC DUCT INTO THE FLOW CONTROL VALVE. AFTER TROUBLE SHOOTING THE PNEUMATIC SYSTEM, IT WAS DETERMINED UNCONTROLLED AIR WAS ENTERING THE PNEUMATIC DUCTS AND OVER PRESSURIZED THE TRANSITION TUBE INTO THE FLOW CONTROL VALVE AND BLEW THE SEAL NEAR THIS VALVE, BLEED AIR BLOWING IN THE AREA OF A HEAT SENSOR LOOP ILLUMINATED THE DUAL BLEED LIGHTS. BY THE PNEUMATIC FLOW SCHEMATIC, THE SOURCE WAS DETERMINED TO BE THE WING ANTI ICE VALVE ON THE RH ENGINE. PARTS WERE SHIPPED AND THE VALVE AND BLOWN SEAL WAS REPLACED. ENGINES AGAIN WERE RAN AND PNEUMATIC/PRESSURIZATION SYSTEM TESTED. NO LEAKS NOTED AND ALL BLEED AIR SHUT OFF/CONTROL VALVES WORKED NORMALLY. THE AIRCRAFT WAS FLOWN TO KELP WITH NO ISSUES REPORTED AND THEN RE INSPECTED. NO DISCREPANCIES/DEFECTS NOTED AT THAT TIME.

SHORTLY AFTER DEPARTURE THE CAPTAIN NOTICED THE COCKPIT LIGHTING OSCILLATING BETWEEN NORMAL AND SLIGHTLY DIMMER. THE CAPTAIN TURNED THE STROBES OFF AND THEN BACK ON TO SEE IF THIS WAS THE SOURCE. NOTHING CHANGED. HE THEN TURNED THE ROTATING BEACON OFF IN WHICH THERE WAS NO CORRECTION. WHEN THE ROTATING BEACON WAS TURNED BACK ON, ALL POWER WAS LOST TO THE NUMBER 1. DUAL FEED BUS. THE CAPTAIN DID AN IMMEDIATE RETURN TO THE MODESTO AIRPORT WITHOUT ANY INCIDENT.  COMMENCED TROUBLESHOOTING BY COMPLETING A TEXTRON DUAL BUS FEEDER - INSPECTION CHECK. ALL CURRENT LIMITERS WERE FUNCTIONAL. RESULTS LED TO A SUSPICION OF A PROBLEM WITH THE DUAL BUS NO. 1 & 2 DIODE PANEL ASSEMBLY. UPON VIEWING THE PANEL, IT WAS IMMEDIATELY APPARENT THAT WIRES WERE BURNT AT THE PANEL ASSEMBLY. THE BURNED WIRES ARE 6 GAUGE IN SIZE. THEY ARE PROTECTED BY 60-AMP CURRENT LIMITERS. AGAIN, THESE CURRENT LIMITERS WERE INTACT YET THERE WAS EXTENSIVE WIRE BURNING.  FEEDER WIRE P5A6, WHICH FEEDS POWER TO DIODE CR2 WAS IN HARD CONTACT WITH DIODE CR1. BURN MARKS ON THE WIRE INDICATE HEAVY CURRENT FROM WIRE P5AG TO DIODE CR1 AT THE POINT OF CHAFING.  PLASTIC INSULATING HAT SECTIONS AND THIN INSULATORS BELONG UNDERNEATH EACH DIODE TO ELECTRICALLY ISOLATE THE DIODES FROM THE METAL HEAT SINK. BOTH HAT SECTIONS WERE COMPLETELY BURNED AWAY. THIS PROVIDED AN OPPORTUNITY FOR THE DIODES TO SHORT TO THE HEAT SINK. THAT CLEARLY HAD HAPPENED.  WIRES P2A6 AND P6A6, NOT READILY VISIBLE DURING NORMAL PHASE INSPECTIONS WERE HIGHLY BURNT.  THE WIRES WERE NUMBERED WITH OLDER MASKING TAPE SO WORK WAS COMPLETED ON THEM AT SOME PREVIOUS AND UNDETERMINED TIME.  THE LOCK WASHERS FOUND ON THE DIODE ATTACHMENT HARDWARE WERE THE STAR WASHER TYPE AND DID NOT HAVE A PLAIN WASHER BETWEEN THE LOCK WASHER AND THE THIN INSULATING WASHER. THE LOCK WASHERS ON THE DIODE ATTACHMENT HARDWARE SHOULD BE THE SPLIT LOCK WASHER TYPE. A TEXTRON CUSTOMER SERVICES ENGINEER PROVIDED US DRAWINGS TO PROPERLY INSTALL THE DIODES. THOSE DRAWINGS INDICATE A SPLIT LOCK WASHER SHOULD BE USED (PN MS35338-44) AGAINST A THIN PLAIN WASHER THEN THE INSULATING WASHER. WE BELIEVE IT IS LIKELY THE LOCK-WASHER COULD HAVE CUT THROUGH THE INSULATION AND PROVIDED CONTINUITY TO THE HEAT SINK. THE BEECH MANUALS DO NOT PROVIDE A BREAKDOWN OF WHAT PROPER ATTACHMENT HARDWARE IS REQUIRED FOR THE DIODES.  DIODE CR1 WAS FOUND TO BE ELECTRICALLY OPEN AND DIODE CR2 WE BELIEVE HAD INTERMITTENT CONTINUITY AS IT WAS FOUND BROKEN ON THE INPUT SIDE THAT THE WIRE P5A6 ATTACHES TO. HOWEVER, BEFORE WE DISTURBED IT, IT PROVIDED SUFFICIENT CONTINUITY DURING THE DUAL BUS FEEDER - INSPECTION CHECK.  THE ROTATING BEACON WAS IN A FAILED CONDITION. OUR THOUGHTS ARE THAT THIS WAS EITHER COINCIDENTAL TO THE INCIDENT OR AN ELECTRICAL CURRENT FOR THE BEACON WAS A "STRAW THAT BROKE THE CAMEL'S BACK."  THE ACTUAL HEAT SINK OF THE RECTIFIER ASSEMBLY IS NORMALLY NEITHER ELECTRICALLY POWERED OR A GROUNDED PART. NYLON WASHERS UNDER THE HEAT SINK ATTACHMENT SCREWS PROVIDE ELECTRICAL ISOLATION. HOWEVER, WITH THE LIKELY CUT DIODE INSULATORS AND / OR WIRE P5A6 CHAFFING HARD AGAINST DIODE CR1, THE HEAT-SINK BECAME CHARGED WITH BUS POWER. WITH THE HEAT SINK AT 28 VOLTS, WE BELIEVE AN AIRCRAFT WOULD STILL OPERATE NORMALLY, THOUGH IT WOULD LACK THE INTENDED PROTECTION OF THE DUAL BUS FEEDER DESIGN.
FOR UN-DETERMINED REASONS, IT APPEARS THAT THE HEAT SINK SHORTED TO THE FRAME (FRAME PN 101-364053-5) THAT IT MOUNTS TO AND PROVIDED A PATH TO GROUND. THE SPACE BETWEEN THE FRAME AND THE HEAT SINK IS JUST SUFFICIENT ENOUGH FOR A DASH 4 WASHER TO SNUGLY FIT AND PROVIDE AN ELECTRICAL PATH FROM THE HEAT SINK TO ITS MOUNTING FRAME.  THOUGH NO BURN MARKS ARE EVIDENT BETWEEN THE HEAT SINK AND THE MOUNTING FRAME, THIS TYPE OF HARDWARE WAS FOUND ON THE FUSELAGE FLOOR BELOW THE HEAT SINK ASSEMBLY AND ITS MOUNT. IN ADDITION, THE FORWARD OUTBOARD MOUNTING AREA FOR THE FRAME TO FUSELAGE STRUCTURE HAS SLIGHT CARBON MARKS. THE FLOOR IS NOT READILY VISIBLE AS THE VIEW IS BLOCKED BY AIR-CONDITIONING DUCTS. ONE COULD ALMOST SAY WE WERE LUCKY TO FIND THE LOOSE HARDWARE.  SO, THERE IS A PLAUSIBLE ELECTRICAL PATH TO GROUND TO PROVIDE A SHORT BUT IT IS NOT READILY APPARENT WHY A CURRENT LIMITER DID NOT BLOW TO PROTECT THE CIRCUIT. OUR THOUGHTS ARE THAT EACH INDIVIDUAL WIRE, P1A6 AND P5A6, THOUGH PROPERLY PROTECTED INDIVIDUALLY BY THEIR RESPECTIVE 60-AMP CURRENT LIMITER, HAD INADEQUATE PROTECTION FOR THE FOLLOWING REASON. THE SHORT TO EACH CIRCUIT AT THE DIODE PANEL ASSEMBLY RENDERED THE DEFECT TO BE PROTECTED BY BOTH CURRENT LIMITERS AT THE SAME TIME. IF THAT WAS THE CASE, THE WIRING IN THIS SITUATION HAD A 120-AMP LIMIT PROTECTION WITH TWO CURRENT LIMITERS ELECTRICALLY IN PARALLEL WHEN IT REALLY STILL NEEDED A 60-AMP LIMIT PROTECTION. THE WIRE COULD THEN BURN BEFORE THE CURRENT LIMITER OPENED. IT WOULD BE GOOD TO HAVE AN ELECTRICAL ENGINEER VERIFY THIS IDEA.  THE FACT THAT -6 GAUGE WIRES BURNED AND NO CURRENT LIMITERS BLEW TO ISOLATE THE DEFECT IS THE REASON WE FEEL IT IS IMPORTANT TO SHARE THIS INFORMATION.
WE HAVE THE FOLLOWING IDEAS TO MITIGATE A REOCCURRENCE OF THIS INCIDENT.  ADD TO THE PHASE 3 INSPECTION, (MM 5-20-03, TABLE 603) TO PAY PARTICULAR ATTENTION TO WIRES ABOVE AND BELOW THE DUAL BUS FEEDER DIODE HEAT SINKS FOR DISCOLORATION INDICATIONS OF OVERHEATING. CURRENTLY THE PHASE 3 INSPECTION REQUIRES A DUAL BUS FEEDER - INSPECTION CHECK. ACCESS TO COMPLETE THAT CHECK IS FROM BELOW A CENTER ISLE FLOORBOARD. THE ACTUAL HEAT SINKS ARE UNDER THE COCKPIT FLOORS. I CAN'T SAY THAT I HAVE EVER LOOKED AT THE WIRES UNDER THE HEAT SINKS AS THIS WOULD EITHER REQUIRE A MIRROR OR A BORESCOPE DUE TO LIMITED ACCESS.  REVISE TEXTRON'S MANUALS TO SHOW THE PROPER WAY TO INSTALL A REPLACEMENT DIODE. THE INFORMATION IS NOT AVAILABLE IN TEXTRON MANUALS.  REVISE TEXTRON'S MANUALS TO ILLUSTRATE PROPER ADEQUATE WIRE CLEARANCE AT THE DIODES.REVISE THE HEAT SINK OR ITS MOUNTING PLATE TO MITIGATE THE POSSIBILITY OF HARDWARE OR FOD ENABLING AN ELECTRICAL PATH BETWEEN THE TWO PARTS.  CHANGE THE DIODE DESIGN IF TODAY'S TECHNOLOGY HAS A LESS DELICATE DESIGN AVAILABLE.

AFTER TAKE OFF EVERYTHING WAS GOING NORMAL UNTIL CROSSING AROUND FL370 CLIMBING FL 400, WHEN WE GOT THE CAS MESSAGE (AMBAR) CABIN ALTITUDE. INCREASING CABIN ALTITUDE UP TO 10000 FT. AT THAT TIME WE STARTED TO RUN THE CHECK LIST WHEN THE RED CABIN ALTITUDE CAS MSG APPEARED ON. AT THAT MOMENT THE CABIN ALTITUDE REACHED 13000 FT. AT THAT TIME WE REQUESTED TO MIAMI CENTER DESCENT TO FL200, THE ATC ASKED IF IT WAS CORRECT THAT ALTITUDE REQUESTED BY US, WE SAID YES WE CONFIRM. WE DID A CONTROL DESCENT DOWN TO FL200 AND THEN 15000 FT. ONCE WE BEGUN THE DESCENT WE DID THE RED CABIN ALTITUDE CHECK LIST BUT WE DIDNT GET ANY RESPONSE WHILE  THE ATC ASKED US WHATS THE REASON OF OUR REQUEST, WE INFORMED ABOUT A PRESSURIZATION PROBLEM AND WE REQUEST TO RETURN TO OUR DEPARTURE AIRPORT KOPF . AT THE DESCENT THE PRESSURIZATION WAS UNDER CONTROL USING THE MANUAL MODE. THE CABIN BECAME TO DESCENT BELOW 10000 FT WITH SEVERAL VARIATION IN THE INSTRUMENT OF THE CABIN CLIMB. FINALLY WE DID A STABLE ILS APPROACH TO THE RUNWAY 09L. MIAMI CENTER ASKED ONCE IF WE REQUIRED ANY ASSISTANCE AT OUR LANDING AND WE SAID NO, WE DIDNT DECLARE THAT ISSUE AS AN EMERGENCY, THE FLIGHT WAS ALWAYS UNDER CONTROL BUT IMPOSSIBLE TO CONTINUE TO OUR INITIAL DESTINATION AIRPORTIN MEXICO  (MMAN). THE ENGINE'S HOT-SECTION WAS THEN REASSEMBLED AS REQUIRED TO FACILITATE REMOVAL OF THE ENGINE FROM THE AIRCRAFT AND RETURN TO OUR REPAIR STATION FOR REPAIR.  UPON INDUCTION OF ENGINE 233606 INTO OUR REPAIR STATION, THE COMPRESSOR SECTION WAS DISASSEMBLED AND THE LIBERATION OF ONE 3RD-STAGE IPC ROTOR BLADE WAS VISUALLY CONFIRMED.  FURTHER DISASSEMBLY OF THE ENGINE REVEALED DOWNSTREAM SECONDARY DAMAGE TO OTHER ENGINE COMPONENTS.

THE FLIGHT WAS GOING AS NORMAL YESTERDAY. ALL SYSTEMS WERE WORKING JUST FINE, AND WE FINISHED OUR CLIMB REACHING A CRUISING ALTITUDE OF FL410 (41,000FT) OVER THE GENERAL LAS VEGAS AREA. THE OUTSIDE AIR TEMPERATURE WAS RELATIVELY COLD YESTERDAY AT ALTITUDE…AROUND -68C TO AROUND -70C. TYPICALLY ONCE THE AIRPLANE GETS COLD SOAKED, THE COCKPIT GETS COLD AND WE TRY TO WARM UP OUR FEET BY USING THE CREW HEAT, WHICH COMES FROM OUR TWO ENVIRONMENTAL CONTROL UNITS (ECU’S). EACH ECU HAS A TURBO AND A SELF CONTAINED OIL SUPPLY TO LUBRICATE THE TURBINE AS IT OPERATES, AS WELL AS CONDENSERS, WATER SEPARATORS, AND HEAT EXCHANGERS IN ORDER TO HELP CONTROL THE TEMPERATURE. AS WE ADJUSTED THE CREW HEAT, THERE OFTEN TIMES WILL BE A LIGHT ODOR ASSOCIATED WITH USING THE HEAT. THIS TIME IT WAS A LOT STRONGER THAN NORMAL, AND MYSELF AND MY CO-CAPTAIN NOTICED SMOKE BUILDING IN THE COCKPIT. THE SMOKE ALSO HAPPENED TO START FILLING UP IN THE CABIN AS WELL TO WHERE THE PASSENGERS NOTICED IT AS WELL. AT THIS POINT, WE TRIED TO ELIMINATE THE PROBLEM BY IMMEDIATELY SETTING THE AIR-CONDITIONING FOR BOTH THE CABIN, AND CREW TO FULL COLD, AND OPENED UP THE AIR GASPERS IN AN ATTEMPT TO HELP REMOVE THE SMOKE. THE SMOKE ITSELF WAS WHITE WITH AN ALMOST BLUEISH HUE, ALMOST CERTAINLY INDICATING IT WAS COMING FROM BURNING OIL, AND NOT ELECTRICAL RELATED. REALIZING THE FLIGHT COULD NOT CONTINUE LIKE THIS, WE IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWED THE MEMORY ITEM PROCEDURES, AND CHECKLISTS FOR AIR CONDITIONING SMOKE. BY THE TIME WE LANDED, THE SMOKE MOSTLY CLEARED AND NEVER GOT WORSE, BUT IT WAS STILL IN THE CABIN.

PATIENT WAS TAKEN INTO THE HOSPITAL, AND PILOT REPOSITIONED BACK TO PARKING PAD.  AFTER SHUTDOWN, PILOT AGAIN INSPECTED THE AIRCRAFT, LOOKING FOR A SOURCE OF THE FUEL SMELL.  AGAIN, NO FUEL LEAKS WERE IN EVIDENCE.  ONCE THE MEDICAL CREW RETURNED, THEY VOICED THEIR CONCERNS TO THE PILOT ABOUT THE FUEL SMELL.  MEDICAL CREW ALSO REPORTED THAT THE PATIENT REPORTED FEELING NAUSEOUS AND VOMITED DURING THE TRANSPORT.  MEDICAL CREW EXPRESSED CONCERNS THAT THE FUEL SMELL MAY HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO THE PATIENT GETTING SICK IN THE AIRCRAFT.  PILOT CALLED THE ON-CALL MECHANIC, DISCUSSED THE SITUATION AND THE MEDICAL CREW CONCERNS.  PILOT AND MECHANIC AGREED TO TAKE THE AIRCRAFT OUT OF SERVICE, SO THAT HE COULD COME IN AND FURTHER INSPECT THE AIRCRAFT.  A WRITE UP WAS ENTERED IN THE LOGBOOK BY THE PILOT, AND AIRCRAFT STATUS REPORTED TO AIRCOM AND COMPLETE FLIGHT.  MECHANIC ARRIVED WITHIN THE HOUR AND CONDUCTED A FURTHER IN-DEPTH INSPECTION. MECHANIC REPORTED A VERY FAINT SMELL OF FUEL WHEN UNDERNEATH THE AIRCRAFT, AROUND THE FUEL SUMP AREA. HE REPORTED CLEANING THE AREA WITH DEGREASER BUT FINDING TO EVIDENCE OF FLUID LEAKS.  PILOT AND MECHANIC TOOK THE AIRCRAFT FOR A TEST FLIGHT TO SEE IF FUEL SMELL HAD GONE AWAY.   DURING THE TEST FLIGHT, THE MECHANIC POSITIONED HIMSELF AT DIFFERENT SPOTS IN THE CABIN TO SEE IS IF HE COULD DETECT ANY SMELL OF OF FUEL.  NONE WERE DETECTED THROUGHOUT THE ENTIRE FLIGHT, WHICH LASTED 16 MINUTES.  AFTER RETURNING TO BASE MECHANIC ASKED ABOUT RECENT FUELING HISTORY OF THE AIRCRAFT. MECHANIC SUSPECTS THAT THE CREW WERE EITHER SMELLING EXHAUST FUMES, OR THAT THE AIRCRAFT HAD BEEN TOPPED OFF IN COLD WEATHER AT NIGHT AND THAT THERMAL EXPANSION OF THE FUEL DURING THE HOTTER DAY MAY HAVE CAUSED SOME FUEL TO ACCUMULATE IN THE FUEL VENTING SYSTEM.  THE FUEL VENTING SYSTEM IS LOCATED BEHIND THE BULKHEAD BY THE PATIENT IN THE CABIN.  AIRCRAFT WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE.

ON 12/29/2023 AT 2025 HOURS, I WAS ATTEMPTING AN ENGINE START AFTER DROPPING OFF A PATIENT AT THE UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO HOSPITAL IN DENVER, CO.  AFTER INITIAL STARTER WIND-UP AND INTRODUCTION OF FUEL, I COULD HEAR THAT THE START WAS SLOWER THAN NORMAL.  AS I MONITORED ENGINE TEMP, I NOTICED A RANGE BETWEEN 860 AND 880 CELSIUS.  THE TEMP WASN'T FALLING AND I WAS NEARING MY LIMITATION OF BEING ABOVE 843 DEGREES CELSIUS FOR MORE THAN TEN SECONDS DURING A START SO I ELECTED TO ROLL OFF THE THROTTLE AND ABORT THE START.  SIMULTANEOUSLY, WE COULD SMELL A STRONG, SULFUR TYPE ODOR COMING INTO THE COCKPIT AND CABIN.  AFTER SHUTDOWN, BATTERY VOLTAGE WAS INDICATING 21.5 WHICH IS BELOW THE ALLOWABLE STARTING REQUIREMENTS.  I MADE THE NECESSARY NOTIFICATIONS AND A NEW BATTERY WAS INSTALLED ON 12/30/2023 AT 0845 HOURS.  THE AIRCRAFT WAS THOROUGHLY INSPECTED FOR ADDITIONAL DEFECTS AND NONE WERE FOUND.

DURING SCENE FLIGHT REQUEST AND ENROUTE TO SCENE, MEDICAL CREW NOTICED AND UNUSUALLY STRONG FUEL SMELL IN THE CABIN AREAS. THE PATIENT SCENE FLIGHT REQUEST CANCELED MOMENTS LATER FROM THE REQUESTERS END, AND WE RETURNED TO BASE (RTB). DURING RTB, THE SMELL SEEMED TO BE WORSE WHEN THE VENT BLOWER OR AIR CONDITIONER WAS ON, AND THE SMELL WAS NOTICEABLY STRONGER IN THE CABIN AREA THAN THE COCKPIT WHICH ONLY HAD A FAINT FUEL SMELL. THERE WERE NO UNUSUAL ENGINE INDICATION AND FUEL FLOW WAS IN THE NORMAL RANGE FOR STRAIGHT AND LEVEL FLIGHT. WHEN POWER WAS REDUCED AND WE WERE ON APPROACH FOR LANDING BACK AT OUR BASE, THE CREW DIDNT NOTICE THE SMELL AS MUCH. THE ENTIRE FLIGHT TIMES WAS ONLY 13 MINUTES, AND THE FUEL SMELL WASN'T PRESENT OR NOTICED UNTIL HALFWAY INTO THE FLIGHT.

MECHANIC WAS PERFORMING A ROUTINE INSPECTION ON THE INERTIAL REELS FOR THE CREW SEATS IN THE CARAVAN. THE AIRCRAFT UNDER INSPECTION WAS PK-MAG, OUR NEWEST CARAVAN. MECHANIC INSPECTED THE BELTS FOR THEIR CONDITION AND THEN TESTED THE REELS BY PULLING THE BELT OUT SLOWLY AND THEN GIVING A FEW SHARP TUGS TO ENSURE THAT THE STOP MECHANISM ENGAGES PROPERLY. THE PILOT SEAT WAS NORMAL, BUT MECHANIC HAD AN ISSUE WITH THE CO-PILOT SEAT. THE SEATS ON THIS AIRCRAFT ARE SIDE-SPECIFIC DUE TO MODS TO HOLD THE POH AND SURVIVAL KIT. ON THE SECOND TUG, THE INERTIA REEL MECHANISM BEGAN MAKING NOISE AND CATCHING AS IT RETRACTED. IT BECAME VERY DIFFICULT TO MOVE THE BELT IN AND OUT OF THE REEL WITHOUT IT LOCKING MANY TIMES ALONG THE WAY. THE MECHANIC TOOK THE LOCK SIDE OF THE REEL APART AND FOUND A BROKEN PLASTIC TAB ON THE SIDE A SMALL GEAR ASSEMBLY THAT HOLDS THE LOCKING PAWL IN THE RETRACTED (FREE) POSITION. THIS PART IS ESSENTIAL WHEN THE PAWL IS UPSIDE-DOWN AND OTHERWISE WILL FALL (GRAVITY) INTO A LOCKED POSITION. THE BELT COULD BE MOVED, BUT ONLY WITH ERRATIC PULLING AND PUSHING. MECHANIC REPLACED THE REEL WITH A SERVICEABLE SPARE AND FINISHED THE INSPECTION. MECHANIC DID NOT FEEL HE TUGGED EXCESSIVELY HARD ON THE BELT, BUT WONDERED HOW LONG THE PLASTIC TAB HAD BEEN IN THE PROCESS OF BREAKING.
